items.title: Decoding Clickbait: The Impact of Clickbait Types and Structures on Cognitive and Emotional Responses in Online Interactions

judge.evidence_topic: This study delves into the influence of clickbait types (hyperbole, insinuation, visual rhetoric, and puzzle) and structures (emotion-label and emotion-laden words) on user cognitive and emotional responses in an online environment.
judge.evidence_empirical: Using electroencephalography with 32 internet-experienced participants, we analyzed how these different clickbait configurations affect engagement and processing.
judge.reason: O artigo é um estudo empírico que utiliza EEG para medir respostas cognitivas e emocionais de usuários a diferentes tipos de clickbait, atendendo aos critérios de inclusão. Os dados extraídos sobre o método e os achados estão corretos e sustentados pelo resumo.

items.title: Click me…! The influence of clickbait on user engagement in social media and the role of digital nudging

judge.evidence_topic: We analyze the impact of clickbait on user interaction on Facebook in the form of liking, sharing and commenting.
judge.evidence_empirical: We use a data set of more than 4,400 Facebook posts from 10 different news sources to analyze how clickbait in post headlines and in post text influences user engagement.
judge.reason: O artigo analisa o impacto do clickbait no engajamento de usuários (curtidas, compartilhamentos, comentários) em posts do Facebook, o que se enquadra no pedido. O estudo é empírico, utilizando um conjunto de dados de 4.400 posts. O método e o achado principal estão corretamente descritos e sustentados pelo resumo.

items.title: You won't believe it! Truth judgments for clickbait headlines benefit (but less so) from prior exposure

judge.evidence_topic: In two high‐powered experiments, we investigated how prior exposure to statements presented in a clickbait format increases the perceived truth of their content.
judge.evidence_empirical: In two high‐powered experiments, we investigated how prior exposure to statements presented in a clickbait format increases the perceived truth of their content. In Experiment 1 ( N = 241)... In Experiment 2 ( N = 291)...
judge.reason: O artigo é um estudo empírico (dois experimentos) publicado em 2023 que investiga o efeito de manchetes clickbait na percepção de verdade dos leitores, atendendo aos critérios de inclusão. O achado extraído é sustentado pelo resumo.

items.title: Exaggerated and Questioning Clickbait Headlines and Their Influence on Media Learning

judge.evidence_topic: To evaluate the impact of clickbait headlines on media learning and article-related beliefs, we conducted two online experiments
judge.evidence_empirical: we conducted two online experiments, each testing a 3 (headline-type: accurate, clickbait-question, clickbait-exaggerated) × 2 (exposure: headline-only, full article) factorial.
judge.reason: O artigo é um estudo empírico (experimentos) que investiga os efeitos de manchetes clickbait na aprendizagem midiática, atendendo aos critérios de inclusão. O método e os achados extraídos estão corretamente descritos e sustentados pelo resumo.

judge.evidence_topic: whether these strategies effectively drive audience engagement
judge.evidence_empirical: rage bait headlines were linked to higher levels of audience engagement, while information bait was associated with lower engagement.

items.title: Shocking secret you won't believe! Emotional arousal in clickbait headlines

judge.evidence_topic: The purpose of this paper is to fill a gap in the literature by providing empirical evidence of how clickbait headlines affect online users’ emotional and behavioral responses, specifically emotional arousal and intention to read news.
judge.evidence_empirical: An experiment was conducted primarily to examine the levels of emotional arousal evoked by two treatment groups of online news headlines, news and clickbait, compared to a neutral control group.
judge.reason: O artigo é um estudo empírico (experimento) sobre os efeitos de manchetes clickbait na excitação emocional e intenção de leitura, sem recorte político. O método descrito no resumo (experimento com eye-tracking e SAM) condiz com o extraído. O tamanho da amostra não consta no resumo. O achado principal está integralmente sustentado pelo texto do resumo.

items.title: Effects of Clickbait Headlines on User Responses: An Empirical Investigation

judge.evidence_topic: This study investigates the influence of a conventional method of delivering news headlines, clickbait, on online users’ perceptions and responses.
judge.evidence_empirical: An experiment was conducted on two groups of news headlines—traditional news and clickbait— to provide empirical evidence of the effects of clickbait on online users.
judge.reason: O artigo é um estudo empírico (experimento) que analisa o impacto de manchetes clickbait na percepção e comportamento de usuários, alinhando-se ao pedido. O método descrito nos dados extraídos condiz com o resumo. Os achados principais relatados nos dados extraídos são sustentados pelo resumo.

items.title: Clickbait-style headlines and journalism credibility in Sub-Saharan Africa: Exploring audience perceptions

judge.evidence_topic: This experimental study, therefore, set out to understand how the audience perceives clickbait-style headlines in relations to media credibility.
judge.evidence_empirical: This experimental study, therefore, set out to understand how the audience perceives clickbait-style headlines in relations to media credibility. judge.reason: O artigo é um estudo experimental empírico que analisa a percepção de leitores sobre a credibilidade de manchetes clickbait, atendendo aos critérios de inclusão. O achado principal está diretamente sustentado pelo resumo.

items.title: Did clickbait crack the code on virality?

judge.evidence_topic: Using the Persuasion Knowledge Model, we predict that clickbait tactics may be perceived by some readers as a manipulative attempt, leading to source derogation where the publisher may be perceived as less competent and trustworthy. This, in turn, may reduce some readers’ intention to share content.
judge.evidence_empirical: Using a controlled experiment, we confirm that high-emotional headlines are shared more and show evidence that clickbait often leads to inferences of manipulative intent and source derogation. We then use a well-known secondary data set containing 19,386 articles from 27 leading online publishers.
judge.reason: O artigo realiza um experimento controlado e uma análise de dados secundários, atendendo aos critérios empíricos. O tema está alinhado com o pedido (efeitos do clickbait em leitores). O achado principal está devidamente sustentado pelo resumo.

items.title: Seeing is not always believing: an exploratory study of clickbait in WeChat

judge.evidence_topic: The purpose of this study is to unpack the antecedents and consequences of clickbait prevalence in online media at two different levels, namely, (1) Headline-level: what characteristics of clickbait headlines attract user clicks and (2) Publisher-level: what happens to publishers who create clickbait on a prolonged basis.
judge.evidence_empirical: the authors collected longitudinal data in collaboration with a leading company that operates more than 500 WeChat official accounts in China.
judge.reason: O artigo é empírico e trata do tema. O método descrito está correto, mas o tamanho da amostra foi informado incorretamente como 'não informado no resumo', quando o resumo cita explicitamente 'more than 500 WeChat official accounts'.

items.title: The mechanism leads to successful clickbait promotion in WeChat social media platforms

judge.evidence_topic: This study aims to examine how the clickbait headlines influence the perceived source credibility, subjective norm, perceived benefit and purchasing intention of customers on social commerce through social media platforms
judge.evidence_empirical: A total of three studies were employed online to test the hypotheses. Study 1 used a single-factor, two-condition (clickbait: yes vs no) between-subject design.
judge.reason: O artigo foca em comércio social e intenção de compra, não em consumo de notícias, que é o recorte temático solicitado pelo pesquisador.

items.title: Semantic structure of clickbait headlines and internet user activities

judge.evidence_topic: Actual interests of the audience — news content readers — focus on such concepts as character, event and chronotope (fields “Celebrities”, “Putin, Incidents”, “News”, “Death”, “Donbas”, “Kazakhstan”, “Crimea”, etc.).
judge.evidence_empirical: The material of the study is 4900 headlines of Russian news media for May 2019, provided by the news aggregator SMI2.

items.title: The curiosity effect: Information seeking in the contemporary news environment

judge.evidence_topic: This research investigates how digital news headlines influence contemporary news information seeking. In two studies (a lab experiment and a field test), we examine how the presentation of news information—traditional, summary news headlines or clickbait, curiosity news headlines—influences the attitudinal and behavioral components of news seeking.
judge.evidence_empirical: In two studies (a lab experiment and a field test), we examine how the presentation of news information—traditional, summary news headlines or clickbait, curiosity news headlines—influences the attitudinal and behavioral components of news seeking.
judge.reason: O artigo é um estudo empírico (experimento e teste de campo) que investiga o efeito de manchetes de curiosidade (clickbait) no comportamento de busca de notícias, sem recorte político. Os dados extraídos estão corretos e são sustentados pelo resumo.

items.title: Pengaruh Berita Clickbait Terhadap Kepercayaan pada Media di Era Attention Economy

judge.evidence_topic: Berita clickbait dapat menurunkan kepercayaan terhadap media. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengidentifikasi apakah terdapat pengaruh berita clickbait terhadap kepercayaan pada media.
judge.evidence_empirical: Metode yang digunakan dalam penelitian ini adalah kuantitatif dengan paradigma positivis. Data penelitian ini dikumpulkan menggunakan kuesioner jenis angket tertutup. Kuesioner disebar kepada 100 responden yang sebelumnya ditentukan menggunakan teknik purposive sampling
judge.reason: O resumo afirma que o estudo encontrou um 'pengaruh positif' (influência positiva) de 28,4% na confiança, enquanto o dado extraído afirma uma 'redução de 28,4%'. A parte sobre os respondentes continuarem confiando na mídia está correta, mas a direção da influência (redução vs. influência positiva) está incorreta.

items.title: English Clickbait Language Features Which Attract Thai Tertiary EFL Learners

judge.evidence_topic: This study explored how likely its Thai participants were to choose to read an article with a clickbait headline, together with how the reasons given for choosing clickbait headlines correspond to the linguistic features found in the headlines.
judge.evidence_empirical: News headlines were presented to 18 participants to rate which news headline they would choose. Then, the rationales behind the selection were elicited using an interview.
judge.reason: O estudo é empírico, focado na reação de leitores a manchetes clickbait, e os achados extraídos refletem fielmente os resultados descritos no resumo.
